Commentary.Commentary: So West Indies need 399 to win or play out two days to retain the Wisden Trophy. England need 10 wickets and have more than 2 days if weather permits to win the series. The hosts have around 23 minutes to try and get a wicket or two. Can West Indies rise from the ashes or will the inevitable happen?

It has been a tough day for West Indies. First they failed with the bat and that disappointment couped with injuries made things more difficult than they already were for the hosts. The bowlers had to toil hard and did not have much success. Gabriel's compromised fitness meant that the visitors got just 5 overs from their strike bowler. Holder too injured his thumb which added salt to the wound. The skipper still managed to get a wicket along with Chase. Rahkeem Cornwall bowled the most overs but without any success. All-in-all a jaded bowling performance from West Indies.

So England have decided they have enough on the board and have declared! The platform is set for them to regain the Wisden Trophy. Having a lead of 233, the openers tookk their time but set the platform with the opening pair of Sibley and Burns adding a slightly slower but steady 114 stand with both openers getting to their fifties. Sibley though departed against the run of play which meant the stage was set for the England skipper to play his T20 game. Root's unbeaten 68 off just 56 balls along with Burns' 90 has zoomed their lead to 398 and with the departure of Burns they decided to declare their innings.

OUT! LBW! Sibley has to depart and he takes a review with him. This is the danger of coming too far across your off stump, you're always vulnerable and that is what has happened here. Good length ball on off and coming back in, Sibley comes across and looks to flick but misses. This time the ball hits him low on his pad. Holder goes up in a confident appeal and the umpire agrees with him and raises his finger. Sibley has a word with his partner and decides to opt for the review. Replay rolls in and Ultra Edge shows flat line as the ball goes past the bat. Time for the Ball Tracker and it shows three reds. The search for the first wicket is over and it is the skipper Holder who has given his side that.
This time Sibley has taken the review. He has been adjudge LBW and to the naked eye he looks like a goner. Let's see if technology comes to his aid.

Ball Tracker then comes and it shows that the ball is clipping the top of middle pole but not enough to overturn. The search for the first wicket continues.
Review time! Holder thinks he has his man but the umpire does not feel so. He has signaled the 'T' and gone upstairs. Let's see if they have got better of this partnership or their search continues.

We are back for the final session of Day 3. The West Indies players are out in the middle. Rory Burns and Dom Sibley will resume their innings for England. Kemar Roach will start the proceedings for the final session of Day 3.
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

West Indies, on the other hand, had a very tough session. Their players struggling for fitness and bowlers struggling to get the breakthrough has seen their heads drop a bit. Holder will need to motivate and inspire his men and will need someone to show some fight in the final session. How will the host play the final session? Will they go on the aggressive or carry on their cautious approach? Join us in the final session to find out.

Time for a drink. The match is slowly but surely going away from the West Indies. But what can they do? If they bowl with fire and get England all out quickly, that would mean enough time for the hosts to get them out as well, in spite of the poor weather. On the other hand, playing for time, hoping that the rain would come, will not help either! Probably, the best way to play would be just enjoy the game. Give your best and hope for the best. It has been a painful 16 overs for West Indies, with Jason Holder and Shane Dowrich getting injured. There was a stumping chance, of Burns, but da Silva could not quite get it done. We are back for the second session. Jason Holder is giving word of motivation to the players in the huddle before they take the field. Rory Burns and Dom Sibley walk out to resume their innings. Kemar Roach to bowl the first over of the new session.
... Day 3, Afternoon Session ...

England had about 20 minutes to survive after the innings break before Lunch and they have done so successfully, with Burns and Sibley both still at the crease. They will look to set the platform for the batters coming in next so that they can go hammer and tongs and swell their lead. Can the West Indies choke them and take some wickets to turn the tide a bit in their favour? Join us after the Lunch break to find out!

The session started with some momentum for the visitors. It looked like they would pull away a bit after Holder and Dowrich avoided the follow-on but it was again just moments rather than a long period of good play from the West Indies. As soon as Stuart Broad came into the attack, he started to rip apart the West Indies. West Indies went from 178 for 6 to 197 all out, with Broad taking all four wickets, completing his 5-fer in the process as well.

Another session goes by, and nothing has changed. England remain unscathed at the end of the first session on Day 3 and are way on top of the West Indies, as they lead now by 182 runs. The visitors will need to perform some sort of miracle now to stay in this game and to have any hopes of retaining the Wisden trophy.

EDGED BUT FALLS SHORT! Holder has hurt himself here. Good length ball around off, Burns looks to defend but does so with soft hands. He gets a thick outside edge which falls short of second slip. Holder gets down and the ball brushes his fingers and goes behind allowing them to take a single. The skipper is down in pain and looks like he has hurt his finger. Replays roll in and show that the ball bounced in front of him and  hit him on the top of his left thumb. That can prove to be a huge problem for the Windies as they need their skipper on the field.
